history.text: ok back to the undo/redo design for the diagram editor. command objects or immutable snapshots of the doc?

Command objects. Each edit becomes an invertible command (MoveNodes, AddEdge, SetStyle) on a history stack, which keeps memory flat on large diagrams and gives you a clean hook for collaboration later. Snapshots are simpler, but they copy the whole document on every small change.
how does undo work once two ppl are editing the same diagram tho

Undo should be per user: each client keeps its own stack and undoes only its own commands, transformed against the remote edits that arrived since. If a remote edit deleted the node your command touched, that command becomes a no-op and is skipped rather than resurrecting the node.

history.text: so given all that, outbox table + relay, or just publish to kafka right after the db commit?

Outbox with a relay. Publishing after the commit loses events whenever the process dies between the commit and the publish, and you can't detect it. The outbox write is part of the same transaction, and the relay gives you at-least-once delivery with ordering per aggregate.
ok im convinced, outbox it is. ill write the ADR myself later
Sounds good. Key points for the ADR: transactional consistency, ordering per aggregate, and at-least-once delivery, which means consumers have to be idempotent.
